evidence.statement: The artifact's answers and explanations align with the supplied source: generative AI creates new content, and the listed marketing, coding, visual-generation, customer-support, and personalized-learning uses are represented accurately.

Distractors are drawn from neighboring source use cases, such as support, coding, visual generation, and learning, making them credible while remaining distinguishable from the target use.
Wrong choices diagnose realistic category-confusion misconceptions, including confusing marketing with support, coding with visual generation, and personalized learning with customer support.

The session includes remembering and understanding items, but the sequence introduces several specific use cases before defining generative AI, so the conceptual foundation arrives after application examples.
The exact sequence repeats mechanics in uninterrupted pairs—two multiple-choice items, two true/false items, two multiple-choice items, two true/false items, and so on—creating a predictable rhythm.
Prompt stems vary across definition, capability, and claim formats, but multiple items reuse the same 'What can...' construction and several true/false items use declarative claims.
The items accurately represent workplace and learning use cases from the source, but they are direct recall questions rather than credible decision or task scenarios.

Explanations and option rationales usually identify the governing category distinction and redirect learners to the better-fitting use case; the true/false items also provide intrinsic and instructional feedback.
The mostly remembering and understanding items fit the unit SLO to identify generative AI and match it to common workplace uses.
The artifact consistently uses source-aligned terms such as generative AI, marketing content, virtual agents, code generation, image and video generation, and personalized learning.
The session is source-faithful and instructive, but its delayed definition and highly patterned mechanic sequence reduce coherence and engagement.
